content.title: What are Constructors?
content.description: A constructor is a special member of a class that is automatically executed when an object is created. Its primary purpose is to initialize the object's data.

content.content: Whenever an object is created using the new keyword, Java automatically calls a constructor. Constructors help initialize instance variables and ensure that every object starts with the required values.

content.title: Why Constructors?
content.content: Constructors eliminate the need to initialize object data manually after object creation, making programs cleaner and more reliable.
Characteristics of Constructors
Constructors have the same name as the class, do not have a return type, and are invoked automatically whenever an object is created.

items.question: Does a constructor have a return type?
items.answer: No. Constructors never specify a return type, not even void.

items.question: Can a constructor have parameters?
items.answer: Yes. Constructors can accept parameters to initialize objects with different values.

items.question: Can a class have multiple constructors?

content.content: Default Constructor
If no constructor is written in a class, Java automatically provides a default constructor. It initializes objects with default values.

content.title: Default Constructor Example
Remember
content.content: Java provides a default constructor only when no constructor is explicitly defined by the programmer.
Parameterized Constructor
A parameterized constructor accepts arguments, allowing objects to be initialized with different values during creation.

content.title: Parameterized Constructor

content.content: Constructor Overloading
Constructor overloading allows multiple constructors in the same class with different parameter lists. This provides multiple ways to create objects.

content.title: Constructor Overloading

content.content: The this Keyword
The this keyword refers to the current object. It is commonly used inside constructors to distinguish instance variables from parameters having the same name.

content.title: Using this Keyword

content.content: Constructor Chaining
Constructor chaining allows one constructor to call another constructor within the same class using the this() statement.

content.title: Constructor Chaining Example

content.content: Constructor vs Method
Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Registering a New Student
content.content: When a new student joins a school, the admission form automatically records the student's name, age, and class. Similarly, a constructor automatically initializes an object's data when it is created.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Constructors, constructor overloading, default constructors, parameterized constructors, the this keyword, and constructor chaining are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can a constructor have a return type?
items.answer: No. Adding a return type turns it into a regular method.

items.question: Why isn't the default constructor available?
items.answer: Because Java does not generate one if any constructor is explicitly defined.

items.question: Can this() appear anywhere inside a constructor?
items.answer: No. It must always be the first statement inside the constructor.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Constructors initialize objects automatically. They share the class name, have no return type, and support overloading for flexible object creation.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Constructor names must match the class name.
Constructors do not have a return type.
The this keyword refers to the current object.

content.question: Which keyword refers to the current object inside a constructor?
Which statement about constructors is correct?
options: Constructors have the same name as the class.
content.answer: Constructors have the same name as the class.
